verdict.rationale: a-Shell keeps user data as ordinary files. It documents its own ways to get them out: the `Get File` Shortcuts action, moving or compressing files to send to other apps, and a plain-JSON theme config. It is also fully open source. There is no documented single 'export everything' feature covering all app data, such as settings and command history, so this is only partial. Missing for 10: a documented complete-data export (history, settings, bookmarks), an explicit statement of export formats, and hands-on corroboration of leaving with all data intact.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: `Put File` and `Get File` are used to transfer files to and from a-Shell.
Create directories, move files, compress them, uncompress them, edit them, run python, lua or Tex on your files, move them to other apps.
Edit the JSON file in Files or a text editor. It uses the Windows Terminal color scheme format
a-Shell is entirely OpenSource, and released under the FreeBSD license.
